# Future Directions — Excluded minors for Z_n-gainable biased graphs

Derived from the Stage-3 analysis and Stage-4 critique of this cycle. The formalised
results (`ZnGain.lean`, `ZnGainSharp.lean`) settle the **parallel-class (digon) slice** of
the Zaslavsky/Funk conjecture over *every* cyclic group `ℤ/n` (n ≥ 2), with sharp threshold
`(n+1)K₂`, and establish a divisibility monotonicity law. The following conjectures push
beyond that slice.

## C1. The full three-minor characterisation for all n ≥ 2

**Conjecture.** For every `n ≥ 2`, a biased graph is `ℤ/n`-gainable iff it contains none of
the minors `(n+1)K₂`, `±K₃`, or `−K₄`.

*The key insight is...* that the necessity of `(n+1)K₂` and the entire parallel-class
sufficiency are already `n`-uniform and primality-free (proved here); what remains is a
*finite, n-independent* obstruction set `{±K₃, −K₄}` coming from 3- and 4-vertex
signed-graph geometry. This suggests the characterisation splits cleanly into a
"counting" part (`(n+1)K₂`, fully formalised) and a "geometric" part (`±K₃`, `−K₄`,
independent of `n`).

*Why now?* The counting part is closed in Lean with sharp thresholds and a divisibility
law, so the open frontier is now precisely isolated to two fixed small minors — a
tractable, well-scoped target rather than an `n`-parametrised family.

## C2. A vertexed biased-graph model that *sees* `±K₃` and `−K₄`

**Conjecture.** Enriching `BiasedGraph` with an explicit incidence (vertex) structure and
re-running the gain/realisation definitions yields `±K₃` and `−K₄` as genuine excluded
minors detectable by a Lean-checkable local certificate (a 3- or 4-vertex unbalanced
configuration with no consistent gain).

*The key insight is...* that the current cycle-only abstraction is provably blind to
`±K₃`/`−K₄` (Stage-3 analysis): these obstructions live in the join of incident triangles,
not in any single cycle. A minimal incidence layer should make them first-class.

*Why now?* We have a working, axiom-clean gain framework and minor relation; adding
incidence is an *extension*, not a rewrite, and the parallel-class proofs give a template
for the realisation/pullback lemmas.

## C3. Divisibility lattice of gainability classes

**Conjecture.** The map `n ↦ {biased graphs gainable over ℤ/n}` is a lattice homomorphism
from `(ℕ_{≥1}, ∣)` into the powerset lattice: gainable-sets are monotone under `∣`, and the
gainable-set for `lcm(m,k)` contains the union of those for `m` and `k`.

*The key insight is...* that `gainable_mono_of_dvd` (proved here) already gives monotonicity
along divisibility via an injective hom `ℤ/m ↪ ℤ/n`; the union/`lcm` step should follow from
the Chinese Remainder embedding `ℤ/lcm ↪ ℤ/m × ℤ/k`.

*Why now?* The injective-hom monotonicity lemma is in place and group-generic
(`gainableBy_of_injective_hom`), so the lattice statement is a direct, testable next step.

## C4. Tightness of the divisibility law (strictness)

**Conjecture.** For `m ∤ n` with `m, n ≥ 2`, there exists a biased graph gainable over `ℤ/m`
but not over `ℤ/n` *and* one gainable over `ℤ/n` but not `ℤ/m`; i.e. the divisibility order
on gainability classes is *exactly* divisibility, with no spurious collapses.

*The key insight is...* that the parallel class `kK₂` already separates moduli by the rule
`gainable ⇔ k ≤ n` (proved in `ZnGainSharp.lean`), while group-structure obstructions (odd
vs. even order elements) separate in the other direction.

*Why now?* The sharp threshold `parallelEdges_gainable_iff` provides ready-made separating
examples in one direction; only the group-structural separator remains to be built.

## C5. Algorithmic excluded-minor testing for the digon slice

**Conjecture.** For the parallel-class family there is a polynomial-time (indeed `O(|E|)`)
certificate of `ℤ/n`-gainability: count balance classes `q` and compare `q ≤ n`; this is
formalisable as a `Decidable` instance equivalent to `¬ IsMinor ((n+1)K₂) G`.

*The key insight is...* that `digon_gainable_iff_card` reduces gainability to a single
cardinality comparison `Fintype.card (Quotient s) ≤ n`, which is decidable.

*Why now?* The equivalence is already proved and `DecidableRel`-parametrised; wrapping it as
a `Decidable (Gainable n (digonGraph s))` instance is a short, high-value formal step that
turns the characterisation into an executable test.
